premises: Fixed by the owner or the canon: star L 1.05 Lsun, orbit 1.02 AU, planet 1.14 Mearth and 1.04 Rearth, 1.6 bar air with 21% O2 (volcanic island, wet fuels), 26 h day, 367 d year. Everything else below is derived from them in order.

violation.what: Life arrived on two seed capsules from outside the planet (the makers), so all of it shares one biochemistry (a porphyrin photosystem, DNA-like heredity, L-amino acids, a nitrogen-fixing symbiont) and one ancestor.
violation.why: Primigenia's own lore (F22, F24; meteor shards, W10). Water and panspermia are allowed in this world because its lore says so; derivation.md forbids them as a default elsewhere.
violation.where_in_play: Any carcass feeds any creature, parts graft between lineages (F24).

items.claim: Star: quiet G1V, 1.05 Lsun, 3.8 Gyr.
items.source: Chosen premise: the art fixes a yellow-white sun.
items.consequence: Sets the energy input to every producer.

items.claim: Orbit 1.02 AU, eccentricity 0.02, tilt 26.5 deg.
Star mass about 1.05 Msun, derived from the 367-day year at 1.02 AU (Kepler III).
items.consequence: A 1.05 Msun star at 3.8 Gyr is consistent with 1.05 Lsun only roughly (stars this massive are somewhat brighter by now); mass is the less certain input.

items.claim: Stellar flux 1.009 times Earth's.
items.consequence: Earth-like energy budget: the producers' photon supply is the same as Earth's, so what differs is air, rock and chemistry.

items.claim: Equilibrium temperature about 255 K at an assumed Bond albedo of 0.30.
items.consequence: Without a greenhouse the island would freeze; the air must supply about 32 K (D9).

items.claim: Surface gravity 1.055 g from 1.14 Mearth and 1.04 Rearth.
items.consequence: Falls and cliffs matter; body-size ceiling is set by oxygen, not gravity (D17).

items.claim: One year is 339 local days of 26 h.
items.consequence: Four seasons of about 85 local days: the plant and breeding calendar.

items.claim: Air 1.6 bar: N2 77%, O2 21%, Ar 1.5%, CO2 0.1%, humid; mean molar mass 28.9 g/mol.
items.source: Chosen premise (owner, F5: 21% O2, wet fuels).
items.consequence: Density, pO2 and drag below all follow from this one number.

items.claim: The air must warm the surface by about 32 K to reach the stated 14 C mean; Earth manages 33 K with a thinner, drier air, so a denser, humid air easily does.
pO2 = 0.336 bar, 1.6 times Earth's.
items.consequence: Large aerobic bodies and costly organs are affordable (F5); fast aerobic decomposition (D28).

items.claim: Air density 1.58 times Earth's sea level.
items.formula: rho = P M / (R T), relative to 1.013 bar, 288 K, 28.97 g/mol
items.consequence: Drag 1.6x (F4), wind force per m/s 1.6x (F19): low heavy bodies on ridges, cheap gliding.

items.claim: Sound speed about 340 m/s at 14 C; F4 says about 345 (within 1.5%).
Atmospheric scale height 8.0 km.
items.consequence: At 2,050 m the pressure is still about 77% of sea level: the summit is thin but breathable.

items.claim: Water boils at 113.3 C at sea level (1.6 bar).
items.consequence: Hot springs and fumarole condensate run hotter than on Earth; microbial mats still stop near 70 C (F23).

items.claim: Hydrogen escape parameter about 7.7 at an assumed 1,000 K exobase (Earth about 7.0): H leaks slowly, heavier gases and He are kept.
items.formula: lambda = v_esc^2 m / (2 k T_exo), r = R + 500 km
items.consequence: A dense N2-O2 air is stable over 3.8 Gyr; reduced H2 does not accumulate, so fuels stay organic and wet.

items.claim: Terminal velocity of a falling body is about 18% lower than on Earth; F4 says about 25%.
items.known_discrepancy: F4 says about 25% lower; the same ratio recomputes to about 18% (v ratio 0.82). Suggested fix: change F4 to 'about 18-20%'. Not changed here (world canon is the owner's).

items.claim: Wind force at a given speed 1.58 times Earth's, matching F19's 1.6.
items.formula: q = rho v^2 / 2 scales with rho

items.claim: Molecular diffusion about 0.63 times Earth's (D scales with 1/P), F16 says 0.6.
items.consequence: Scent trails last longer in still air; the dawn-and-fog sense (F16).

items.claim: A 1.2 Luna moon at 450,000 km orbits in 32.4 days; F6 says 29.7. About 425,000 km would give 29.7 days.
items.known_discrepancy: The 29.7 d month and the 450,000 km distance in F6 disagree by 9% (sidereal 32.4 d; the synodic month would be longer still). Fix: set the distance to about 425,000 km, or call 29.7 d a rounded figure. Tides (F13) are only mildly affected. Not changed here.

items.claim: Mean lapse 6.2 K/km lies between the moist-adiabatic range and the dry adiabat g/cp = 10.3 K/km.
items.formula: dry adiabat = g / cp, cp about 1005 J/kg/K
items.consequence: Snow above about 1,750 m in winter (3 C annual mean there) and the UV zone of the high slopes (F14).

items.claim: O2 21% is above the 18% open-fire threshold (Balbi and Frank 2023) and below runaway burning; wet fuels keep wildfire a drought-year event.
items.source: lore/rules/technosphere.md; reference balbi_frank_2023_oxygen_bottleneck. Upper bound 30% is an estimate.
items.consequence: Open fire is available (technosphere path open); creature flame is affordable (flame lineage burns raw sulfur, F26).

items.claim: Hotspot volcanism (F7) keeps fumaroles and seeps supplying reduced sulfur (H2S, S0) that meets the 21% O2: H2S + 2 O2 -> SO4(2-) + 2 H+ releases roughly 800 kJ/mol, enough to feed sulfur-oxidising chemosynthetic producers.
items.source: Standard free energy of sulfide oxidation by O2 (textbook: Madigan, Brock Biology of Microorganisms); value from memory, unverified.
items.consequence: Producers that do not need light: crusts at fumaroles (costra_de_azufre), vent seeps in the shallows, iron and sulfur films in flooded lava tubes (F9).

items.claim: One photosystem from the seed (F24) and UV 1.15x at the star, 0.9x at sea level and 1.4x at 2,000 m (F14): producers are green by ancestry, with red-purple UV screens on the high slopes and black melanin-like crusts where UV is highest.
items.source: F25 pigment-signal rule; UV screening pigments as in Earth alpine plants and lichens.
items.consequence: Colour is an honest signal (altitude, alkaloids); black and red producers exist.

items.claim: Shallows are turbid (visibility under 10 m, F20): sediment and plankton absorb blue-violet and leave a narrow yellow-green to red window, so deeper shallow producers carry red and brown accessory pigments (as red algae and cyanobacteria do on Earth).
items.source: Kirk, Light and Photosynthesis in Aquatic Ecosystems (3rd ed., 2011), coastal water types; chromatic adaptation in red algae. From memory, unverified.
items.consequence: Red and brown (non-green) producers in the shallows and the sunken cave mouth.

items.claim: Energy passes up one level at about 10% (Lindeman 1942; Pauly and Christensen 1995). Endotherms keep only about 1-2%, so warm-blooded predators are rarer than a pure 10% rule says. Starting value, to be checked by tracker test L-TROPHIC.
items.consequence: Pyramid spawn weights: apex rare, grazers common (docs/lore/primigenia-food-web.md).

items.claim: Carnivore biomass is about 1% of the prey biomass (Carbone and Gittleman 2002: about 90 kg of carnivore per 10,000 kg of prey). On an island of roughly 35 km2 (a 2,050 m cone about 3.5 km in radius, estimated) with about 5,000 kg/km2 of large herbivores, all large predators together weigh under 2 t: a handful of apex adults (about 6 at 250 kg), not packs.
items.source: carbone_gittleman_2002_carnivore_density; island area and prey density are estimates.
items.consequence: Apex animals are named individuals and set pieces, with very low spawn weight; two or three apex species are all the island can feed.

items.claim: Carcasses float and drift ashore (F20) and any carcass can feed any creature (F24): a shore scavenger guild, plus soaring scavengers on thermals, where gliding in dense air is cheap (F4).
items.consequence: At least three scavenger niches: wrack and carcass line, forest floor, highland thermals.

items.claim: Wet fuels and rare fire (F5) mean litter and dead wood are not burned off but rotted; pO2 1.6x (D10) speeds aerobic decay: a large decomposer guild of fungi and detritivores (litter, dung, wrack, wood, cave guano).
items.consequence: At least three decomposer niches in the forest, meadow, shore and caves.

items.claim: One biochemistry for all lineages (F24) lets a parasite use hosts across lineages; dense herds (rondo bunches) and wet air favour ectoparasites, and the shared nitrogen-fixing symbiont is not a barrier.
items.consequence: Ectoparasite on herds, parasitoid on insects, gill parasite in the shallows, one parasitic plant: each gives the player a cleaning or avoidance job.

items.claim: The island radiation (F27) left niches empty (insect herbivores, pollinators, scavengers, apex, parasites), which the batch fills; island rules produce giants and dwarfs.
items.consequence: The 2026-11-21 random batch (docs/lore/primigenia-food-web.md).

audit: Recomputed by tools/lore/derivation.py (run by tools/lore/validate.py). Two known discrepancies in the canon are reported as warnings: D16 (terminal velocity F4) and D19 (moon period F6).
